content.text: {"scores": {"center": 1, "craft": 4, "facts": 4, "age_fit": 3, "continuity": 4, "delight": 3}, "evidence": {"center": "Phoenix is fully active only in Chapter 1 (presses the brick, \"Uh oh,\" asks Ole what he's making, pulls the duck). After that every individual line or action goes to Cruz, often twice in a row where Phoenix plainly belongs (\"Cruz grabbed Cruz's hand,\" \"Cruz carried planks. Cruz handed out nails,\" \"said Cruz, with a big grin\"). Phoenix's only later presence is group lines (\"the boys yelled\"), so the worst-covered child is active in 1 of 10 chapters and silent for nine in a row. No likes were stated, so there is no further deduction.", "craft": "Strong shape: a cold open at a wobbly home tower, the glowing-brick device, a real problem (\"The top brick fell right off. Plink!\") paid off by the tubes breakthrough, and a callback ending where the tower just goes \"CLICK. And it held.\" Chapters 8 and 9 are thin time-skip vignettes with no beat beyond looking and pointing.", "facts": "The 1932 toys, 1934 'leg godt' name, the 1947 machine, Automatic Binding Bricks, the January 28, 1958 patent, Kjeld as tester, LEGOLAND 1968 and the minifigure in 1978 are all correct, and the True Facts list matches the story. However, the 1947 machine is shown popping out bricks on the spot, though the first bricks came around 1949. The tube design is also credited to a visiting child with no in-story hint that this part is make-believe.", "age_fit": "Word count (1538) is in range, and the short sentences and sound words (CLUNK. HISSSS. POP!) suit Band A. But the fire chapter, with the boys woken by shouting, \"Orange flames danced in the dark\" and the workshop burning while they watch, exceeds the Band A peril level of none, even though it resolves within the chapter. The \"Nobody has money\" framing also skews older than the band.", "continuity": "This is a first story with no bible. It is docked for internal inconsistency: the two children's names are repeatedly swapped or duplicated. The glowing brick also turns up \"in Cruz's pocket\" at the end, although Phoenix pressed it and nobody ever pocketed it.", "delight": "The prose has good read-aloud rhythm (\"He pulled. It held. He shook. It held.\") and a warm \"Play well\" refrain. But a parent reading aloud will stumble on lines like \"'How about Super Awesome Toy Company?' said Cruz. 'How about Duck Company?' said Cruz\" and \"Cruz grabbed Cruz's hand,\" which read as errors and break the spell."}, "caps_applied": ["none"], "disqualified": false, "overall": 3.1, "editor_notes": ["Restore Phoenix in every chapter. Reassign the duplicated Cruz lines (the duck-company name, grabbing Cruz's hand, handing out nails, the second brick in Ch4, the final 'Kids like us') and give Phoenix his own action in Chs 5-9, such as playing with Kjeld, testing the minifigure, or spotting a LEGOLAND model.", "Soften the fire for Band A. Have the boys arrive the morning after, looking at the ashes with Ole, so the resilience beat stays without flames in the dark and children fleeing at night.", "Give Chapters 8 and 9 a real beat (a choice, a hands-on moment or a shout-along), and hedge Cruz's tube idea with a light nod that Godtfred's team really worked it out. Also fix the pocketed-brick continuity."], "best_moment": "He pulled. It held. He shook. It held. He turned it upside down and shook it really hard.", "worst_moment": "Cruz grabbed Cruz's hand, and they ran outside with everyone else."}
